title: Connect a data source and query it

blocks.content: A system you already run holds your data. You'll connect Grafana Cloud to it, test the connection, and run a first query. The data stays where it is — nothing gets copied in.
First, add the connection. You need the **Admin** role in your stack:
Search for the system that holds your data, for example InfluxDB or CloudWatch, then open it from the results.
blocks.tooltip: Type the name of the system you already run. The results filter as you type.

blocks.content: On your data source's page, click **Add new data source**.
Name the connection something you'll recognize later.

Fill in the connection details. The fields depend on your system, but every data source asks two things: where the data lives, and how to sign in. Type credentials yourself — this guide never fills them for you.
Click **Save & test**. It saves the connection and checks that it works.
Your data source is connected and tested.
Now confirm you can query it:
Open the picker and choose the data source you just added.
blocks.tooltip: Every query runs against one of your connected data stores. This picker chooses which one.

blocks.content: The query editor below the picker is specific to your data source, in its own query language — data that lives in InfluxDB is queried in InfluxQL, for example. Start small: ask for one thing you know your system holds.
Click **Run query**. The result comes back drawn below.

You queried your own data in place — nothing was copied into Grafana Cloud, so this connection doesn't add to the usage Grafana Cloud bills for. When a query is worth keeping, build a dashboard from it.
